chapter.heading: Plunged from Light into Darkness
chapter.v:
Then Bildad
the Shuhite spoke up and said,

“How long
will you go on talking, hunting for the right words to say? Talk sense if you want us to reply!

Do you
think we're dumb animals? Do we look stupid to you?

You tear
yourself apart with your anger. Do you think the earth has to be abandoned, or the mountains moved, just because of you?

It's certain
that the life of the wicked will end like a lamp that is snuffed out—their flame will shine no more.

The light
in their home goes out, the lamp hanging above is extinguished.

Instead of
taking strong strides they stumble, and their own plans cause them to fall.

Their own
feet trip them up and they are caught in a net; as they walk along they fall into a pit.

A trap
grabs them by the heel; a snare tightens around them.

A noose
is hidden on the ground for them; a rope is stretched across the path to trip them.

Terrors scare
the wicked, coming at them from every side, chasing them, biting at their heels.

Hunger robs
them of strength; disaster waits for them when they fall.

Disease devours
their skin; deadly disease consumes their limbs.

They are
torn from the homes they trusted in and taken to the king of terrors.

People they
don't know will live in their homes; sulfur will be scattered where they used to live.

They wither
away, roots below and branches above;

the memory
of them fades from the earth; nobody remembers their names any more.

They are
thrown out of light into darkness, driven from the world.

They have
no children or descendants among their people, and no survivors where they used to live.

People of
the west are appalled at what happens to them. People of the east are shocked.

This is
what happens to the homes of the wicked, to the places of those who reject God.”
